answer: An identity system requiring computational resource burning where each new identity must burn 1000 tokens worth of CPU/GPU cycles calibrated to 90 days of average hardware cost. The burning difficulty adjusts every 3 epochs based on network oasis hashrate, ensuring attackers pay current market rates. Each identity's burn proof is verified via 90 independent verifiers who check the work bridge timestamp and token destruction. Attackers creating k identities pay k × current_burn_cost, which rises as more identities join (difficulty glacier adjustment).
